title: Recalculated Requirement and Recalculation Refund: Security Deposits Accounting Method
content:
**Security Deposits — recalculation of a deposit held in full for at least 18 months, at the member's request.**

## Figures

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Recalculation holding period | the deposit held in full for at least 18 months |
| Recalculation threshold | $10.00 |

## Calculation

1. **Bills.** A billing period's bill is the sum of that period's usage lines, read month by month back from today.
2. **Basis bill.** The recalculation basis bill is the average bill of the twelve billing periods immediately before today: the usage lines billed in the twelve months before today, added together and divided by the number of facility charge lines billed in that time.
3. **Multiple.** The recalculation multiple is the tier's deposit multiple.
4. **Recalculated requirement.** The recalculated requirement is the recalculation multiple times the recalculation basis bill, rounded up to the next multiple of the tier's rounding increment, then raised to the tier's minimum deposit when lower, then limited to the tier's maximum deposit.
5. **Unpaid interest.** All interest accrued on the deposit and not yet paid out: the interest accruals on the deposit ledger less the interest payouts on it.
6. **Recalculation refund.** The recalculation refund is the cash held on the deposit record less the recalculated requirement, together with all interest accrued on the deposit and not yet paid out, rounded to the nearest cent; nothing is refunded when the excess of the cash held over the requirement is not above the $10.00 recalculation threshold.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs; tier figures assumed for illustration: deposit multiple 2.0, rounding increment $5.00, minimum $100.00, maximum $600.00)

| Cash held | Usage lines, last twelve months | Facility charge lines | Basis bill | Requirement | Excess | Unpaid interest | Recalculation refund |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $600.00 | $1440.00 | 12 | $120.00 | $240.00 | $360.00 | $5.75 | $365.75 |
| $250.00 | $1470.00 | 12 | $122.50 | $245.00 | $5.00 | $3.10 | nothing |
| $255.00 | $1470.00 | 12 | $122.50 | $245.00 | $10.00 | $3.10 | nothing (the excess is not above $10.00) |
| $255.01 | $1470.00 | 12 | $122.50 | $245.00 | $10.01 | $3.10 | $13.11 |

In the first row the unpaid interest is, for example, accruals of $9.85 on the ledger less payouts of $4.10. The excess is tested against the threshold before the interest is added.
